winner.text: Stop losing 3 hours every single day to this.
winner.reasoning: This hook directly quantifies the pain creators/marketers experience, making the problem impossible to ignore. It uses 'every single day' to emphasize the recurring nature of the problem, which resonates with pre-production tool users who are frustrated by lost productivity and want an immediate solution.

runner_up.text: 3 hours wasted. Watch what changed everything.
runner_up.reasoning: Safe but effective—it mirrors the exact narrative of the reel while creating intrigue about the solution. Less confrontational than the winner, making it accessible to users not yet convinced they have a problem.

script.script:
[HOOK - 0-3 sec]
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Stop losing 3 hours every single day to this.]

[PAUSE]

[PROBLEM - 3-7 sec]
You're manually organizing shots, managing timelines, hunting for footage. Again.
[CUT]
It's eating your entire pre-production day.

[VALUE - 7-20 sec]
Our tool cuts that down to 30 minutes.
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Shot lists → storyboards → shot references]
One place. Drag, drop, organize.
[PAUSE]
No more scattered files. No more wasted time.

[CUT]

[CTA - 20-23 sec]
Follow for more ways to actually get your day back.
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Follow for more]
script.viewer_takeaway: Pre-production tool saves 2.5+ hours daily by centralizing shot organization, storyboarding, and asset management in one intuitive interface.

cover_options: Close-up of frustrated creator staring at multiple open windows/tabs, clock visible showing 3 hours passing. Bold red text overlay: 'Stop losing 3 hours every single day to this.' High contrast, urgent energy.

Split-screen: left side shows chaotic desktop with scattered files/folders, right side shows clean organized interface. Text: 'Stop losing 3 hours every single day to this.' Clean vs. messy visual metaphor.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Close-up of creator looking stressed at cluttered workspace. Multiple windows open, files scattered. Use red accent color. Quick zoom or shake for emphasis. Pause for 1 sec after text appears.
frame_plan.on_screen_text: Stop losing 3 hours every single day to this.

frame_plan.visual_direction: B-roll montage: hands dragging files between folders, timeline scrubbing back and forth, browser tabs multiplying. Fast cuts (0.5-1 sec each). Show frustration through frantic hand movements.
Wide shot of creator at desk, head in hands. Clock or time-lapse showing hours passing. Overlay text in white, bold sans-serif. Cut to black for emphasis.
frame_plan.on_screen_text: It's eating your entire pre-production day.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Demo shot: drag-and-drop interaction showing shot list being created. Smooth, satisfying motion. Use brand color. Text appears in bold, confident tone. Show speed/efficiency.
frame_plan.on_screen_text: Our tool cuts that down to 30 minutes.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Screen recording of tool in action: user dragging shots into storyboard layout, files consolidating into single organized interface. Show 2-3 quick transitions between features. Clean UI, minimal motion blur. Keep pace brisk but readable.
frame_plan.on_screen_text: Shot lists → storyboards → shot references. One place. Drag, drop, organize.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Before/after split-screen or transition: chaotic workspace (left/top) → organized, clean interface (right/bottom). Use motion wipe or fade. Show creator smiling/relieved. 1 sec pause on final clean state.
frame_plan.on_screen_text: No more scattered files. No more wasted time.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Creator looking at camera, nodding or pointing at camera with friendly energy. Text appears bottom-right or center. Bright, direct eye contact. End on creator's face or cursor hovering over Follow button. Hold for 1 sec.

assets_needed: Cluttered desktop/workspace b-roll (multiple windows, scattered files, browser tabs)
Hands dragging files between folders (macro or close-up)
Clock or time-lapse footage (showing 3 hours passing)
Creator with head in hands / fatigued pose
Screen recording of tool demo (shot list → storyboard → organization workflow)
Creator looking at camera, smiling/relieved (direct-to-camera final shot)
Brand color palette (for text overlays and accents)
Sans-serif bold font (white, for on-screen text)
Sound design: notification pings, whoosh effects for file movements, satisfying 'complete' sound for demo

justifications.clarity: Hook lands immediately with specific time loss (3 hours), problem is concrete (scattered files/timelines), solution is quantified (30 minutes)—no ambiguity on what the tool does.
justifications.retention: Problem-to-solution arc is tight, but demo section (10-16 sec) risks losing attention if screen recording feels too fast or UI isn't visually compelling enough to hold non-users.
justifications.save_potential: Core structure is sound: relatable pain → specific solution → before/after proof—easy to edit, rescope, or repurpose for different creator segments.
justifications.shareability: Solves a real workflow problem, but lacks the wow factor or surprise twist that makes creators tag peers; feels functional rather than 'stop-scroll-and-send' viral.
justifications.audience_fit: Directly targets video/film creators in pre-production phase—exact pain points (organizing shots, managing timelines, file chaos) match researched workflow friction.
justifications.cta_strength: Follow-only CTA is too passive and doesn't create urgency; no mention of early access, waitlist, discount, or next step—leaves engaged viewers without a conversion lever.

weaknesses.issue: CTA is vague and low-friction to a fault—'Follow for more' doesn't capitalize on viewers already sold on the 30-minute time save.
weaknesses.fix: Replace final CTA text with: 'Tap the link in bio to see it in action' or 'Follow → check our website for free trial.' Adds friction but directs high-intent users to signup/demo, not just follower growth.

weaknesses.issue: Demo section (10-16 sec) assumes viewers understand what 'shot list → storyboard → shot references' means visually; jargon-heavy for creators unfamiliar with the tool's UI.
weaknesses.fix: Add brief labels during screen recording: 'Add shots here' (pointer/highlight), 'Auto-organize into storyboard' (drag animation), 'One searchable library' (folder icon close-up). Make each step obvious, not assumed.

weaknesses.issue: No social proof or differentiation—viewers don't know if this is better than existing tools (Frame.io, Adobe, Notion templates); video relies purely on emotion.
weaknesses.fix: Add 1-2 sec overlay at 18-20 sec: 'Built for creators, not editors' or 'Free forever' or 'Used by 500+ productions'—gives reason to choose *this* tool over alternatives or DIY workarounds.

captions: Spending 3+ hours organizing shots before you even press record? Our tool cuts pre-production setup to 30 minutes. Shot lists → storyboards → one organized space. No more tab chaos. Follow for the full walkthrough—link in bio if you're ready to actually get your day back.

If you're manually organizing footage across 5 different apps, this is for you. Watch how we condensed the entire pre-production workflow into one drag-and-drop interface. Stop losing half your day to file management. Follow + DM 'TOOL' for early access.
growth.final_call_reason: Concept and audience fit are strong (8-9), but CTA is too soft and demo lacks visual clarity for conversion; fix the call-to-action to point to signup/trial and add UI labels to the tool demo before posting.
